title: Parampare — the heritage board
subtitle: carved sheesham & tamarind seeds
intent: Counting is the strategy: watch for fours, chain the sowing, and gather the larger harvest.

start.text: Two rows of seven pits, six seeds in each. Lift a pit, sow one seed per hole; whenever a hole holds four, they are yours. Count carefully — this game was taught to sharpen young minds.
The old grandmothers used this board to teach arithmetic and patience. The seeds do the counting; you do the planning.

capture.text: A pit reaches four and the seeds are gathered into your store. The whole art is engineering those fours — on your side or the other's.
Four seeds harvested. Notice how a well-chosen pit sends a chain of drops that ripens hole after hole.
Counted and captured. Resource management, one seed at a time — spend a big pit where it will make the most fours.

win.text: The board is bare and your store holds the most. You out-counted your rival — the true lesson of Alaguli Mane.

lose.text: The harvest is in and the other store is fuller. Count further ahead next round — the fours were there to be made.
